title: Valletta
summary: Valletta is a fortified city on a peninsula between two harbours in Malta. The Knights of St John founded it in 1566, soon after the Siege of Malta in 1565, as a planned late Renaissance city. It became Malta's capital in 1570 and was later inscribed as a World Heritage site.

importance.justification: Planned Renaissance fortress capital of Malta, with major regional military and heritage significance.

sources.title: City of Valletta - UNESCO World Heritage Centre
Valletta | Malta’s Historic Capital City & Map | Britannica

reviewer_note: Founding year 1566 comes from UNESCO. Britannica gives only the 1565 siege and 1570 as the date it became capital. Sources do not state an exact founding day. A Japanese UNESCO text says the Order built it in 1565, which differs from the 1566 date. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from UNESCO, Encyclopaedia Britannica; quotes machine-checked.)
